days.label: 2 Kings 10 to 11
days.key: Howbeit from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, wherewith he made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, the golden calves that were in Beth-el, and that were in Dan.
days.s: After Jehu has Ahab’s house and Baal’s worshippers put to death, the chapter turns to the worship he left standing; Rashi, on 10:29, reads his holding to the calves as fear that the kingdom would return to David’s house, as Jeroboam had feared.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on 2 Kings 10:29, Hebrew (The Metsudah Tanach series, Lakewood) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 12 to 14
days.key: But the LORD was gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and had respect unto them, because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, neither hath He cast them from His presence until now.
days.s: Between Elisha’s death and Hazael’s, the chapter pauses on why Israel, oppressed by Aram through all of Jehoahaz’s reign, is spared; Metzudat David, on 13:23, reads ‘until now’ as for ever, since each reader of the verse, in his own day, says ‘until now’.
days.src: Metzudat David, commentary on 2 Kings 13:23, Hebrew (On Your Way) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 15 to 16
days.key: And the LORD smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a house set apart. And Jotham the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
days.s: At the head of a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right yet is stricken; Metzudat David, on 15:5, reads the ‘house set apart’ as release from the toil of governing, kingship counting, as the sages say, as servitude, and Rashi, on 15:5, as a house among the graves, the dead being called free.
days.src: Metzudat David and Rashi on 2 Kings 15:5, Hebrew (On Your Way; the Metsudah Tanach series) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 17 to 18
days.key: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, yet not as the kings of Israel that were before him.
days.s: Opening Israel’s last reign, the chapter gives its verdict on Hoshea; Rashi, on 17:2, reads the difference as his removing the guards posted since Jeroboam’s days against pilgrimage, so when Israel still would not go up, with no king to blame, their exile was sealed.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on 2 Kings 17:2, Hebrew (the Metsudah Tanach series, Lakewood N.J.) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 19 to 21
days.key: ‘Remember now, O LORD, I beseech Thee, how I have walked before Thee in truth and with a whole heart, and have done that which is good in Thy sight.’ And Hezekiah wept sore.
days.s: Told by Isaiah that he will die, the sick Hezekiah turns to the wall and prays; Radak, on 20:3, reads ‘walked before Thee’ as the service of the heart, which he names first, and only then the deeds he has done.
days.src: Radak, commentary on 2 Kings 20:3, Hebrew (Radak on Nach) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 22 to 23
days.key: And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe: ‘I have found the book of the Law in the house of the LORD.’ And Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
days.s: Sent by Josiah about the money for the Temple’s repair, Shaphan hears the high priest’s news; Rashi, on 22:8, reads the find as a scroll hidden under a course of stones when Ahaz burned the Torah, and Radak, on 22:8, as the scroll lying in its place beside the ark, the Torah forgotten in Manasseh’s long reign.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, the Metsudah Tanach series, Lakewood N.J.) and Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach), on 2 Kings 22:8, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: 2 Kings 24 to Isaiah 1
days.key: Come now, and let us reason together, Saith the LORD; Though your sins be as scarlet, They shall be as white as snow; Though they be red like crimson, They shall be as wool.
days.s: After the LORD refuses Judah’s offerings and bids it cease from evil and plead for the widow, an appeal follows; Rashi, on 1:18, reads it as God and Israel weighing together who wronged whom, hope of repentance still held out, and Ibn Ezra, on 1:18, as the prophet bidding Israel join him in accepting God’s rebuke.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, Friedlander, London 1877), on Isaiah 1:18, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 2 to 5
days.key: And the harp and the psaltery, the tabret and the pipe, And wine, are in their feasts; But they regard not the work of the LORD, Neither have they considered the operation of His hands.
days.s: The chapter’s second woe falls on those who drink from early morning into the night; Radak, on 5:12, reads the LORD’s work as Torah and the words of the wise, which the idle rich neglect for music and wine, and Ibn Ezra, on 5:12, as the calamities God brought on Israel when the ten tribes went into exile.
days.src: Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, Friedlander, London 1877), on Isaiah 5:12, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 6 to 9
days.key: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they, seeing with their eyes, and hearing with their ears, and understanding with their heart, return, and be healed.’
days.s: Sent in the throne vision, the prophet is charged to harden the people until their land lies waste; Rashi, on 6:10, reads the hardening as their own doing, refusing to hear the prophets for fear they might understand, repent and be cured.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on Isaiah 6:10, Hebrew (On Your Way) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 10 to 13
days.key: And it shall come to pass in that day, That the remnant of Israel, And they that are escaped of the house of Jacob, Shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; But shall stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
days.s: Foretelling Assyria’s fall once God has finished His work on Zion, the prophet turns to those who survive; Rashi, on 10:20, takes the smiter as Egypt’s kings, their first oppressors, and Radak, on 10:20, as Assyria’s king, on whom Ahaz leaned, since a man leaned on exacts tribute while God asks only trust in truth.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach), on Isaiah 10:20, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 14 to 18
days.key: My heart crieth out for Moab; her fugitives reach unto Zoar, a heifer of three years old; for by the ascent of Luhith With weeping they go up; for in the way of Horonaim they raise up a cry of destruction.
days.s: In the burden of Moab, its cities laid waste in a night, its people wail on every height; Rashi, on 15:5, reads it as the prophet’s own grief, a prophet of Israel lamenting the calamity of another nation, and Radak, on 15:5, as the prophet voicing what each Moabite will say.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach), on Isaiah 15:5, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 19 to 22
days.key: Therefore said I: ‘Look away from me, I will weep bitterly; Strain not to comfort me, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.’
days.s: In the burden of the Valley of Vision, the city’s rulers have fled and its people are taken bound; Rashi, on 22:4, reads ‘look away’ as God’s words to the ministering angels, and Radak, on 22:4, as the prophet’s words to those who would comfort him.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach), on Isaiah 22:4, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 23 to 27
days.key: With my soul have I desired Thee in the night; Yea, with my spirit within me have I sought Thee earnestly; For when Thy judgments are in the earth, The inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
days.s: In Judah’s song of the strong city, the words turn from the people’s waiting in the way of God’s judgements to a single voice; Rashi, on 26:9, reads ‘in the night’ as the exile, which is like night, and Metzudat David, on 26:9, as the hour when the mind is free of troubling thoughts.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Metzudat David (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Isaiah 26:9, Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 28 to 30
days.key: For it is precept by precept, precept by precept, Line by line, line by line; Here a little, there a little.
days.s: With priest and prophet reeling from wine, the chapter asks whom one shall teach; Rashi, on 28:10, reads it as the people setting an idolatrous precept against each one the prophet brings, and holding theirs weightier, and Ibn Ezra, on 28:10, as speech fit for a small child, taught as writing is taught.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, Friedlander’s edition, London 1877), on Isaiah 28:10, Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 31 to 35
days.key: Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; And, ye that are near, acknowledge My might.
days.s: Between God’s rising against the peoples and the fear of Zion’s sinners, the chapter turns to its hearers; Rashi, on 33:13, reads the near as penitents newly drawn close, the far as those faithful from their youth, and Radak, on 33:13, takes the near as those in the Assyrian camp, made to know the might that struck them.
days.src: Rashi (Hebrew, On Your Way) and Radak (Hebrew, Radak on Nach), on Isaiah 33:13, Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 36 to 38
days.key: The living, the living, he shall praise Thee, As I do this day; The father to the children shall make known Thy truth.
days.s: Hezekiah’s writing on his recovery sets the living against the nether-world; Radak, on 38:19, reads it as reason to lengthen life, since God, whom thanks do not profit, made humankind and wills that they live, know His kindness and give thanks.
days.src: Radak, commentary on Isaiah 38:19, Hebrew (Radak on Nach) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 39 to 42
days.key: But they that wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; They shall mount up with wings as eagles; They shall run, and not be weary; They shall walk, and not faint.
days.s: The chapter that sets the unwearied Creator against youths who faint and fall closes on this verse; Ibn Ezra, on 40:31, reads the renewal as fresh strength sent by God before the first is spent.
days.src: Ibn Ezra, commentary on Isaiah 40:31, Hebrew (Friedlander’s edition, London 1877) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 43 to 45
days.key: I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil; I am the LORD, that doeth all these things.
days.s: Closing the LORD’s address to Cyrus, which denies any God beside Him, the verse pairs opposites; Ibn Ezra, on 45:7, takes ‘create’ as decree, darkness as mere absence of light, and evil as war or sickness, named because God strengthens Cyrus and weakens Babylon’s king.
days.src: Ibn Ezra, Commentary on Isaiah, on Isaiah 45:7, Hebrew (Friedlander, London 1877), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 46 to 50
days.key: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction.
days.s: Midway through rebuking obstinate Jacob, the LORD recalls Israel’s trials; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the refiner’s, who removes all the dross, for had He done so few would have remained, the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off.
days.src: Radak, Commentary on Isaiah, on Isaiah 48:10, Hebrew (Radak on Nach), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 51 to 55
days.key: Behold, My servant shall prosper, He shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
days.s: Before onlookers tell of a servant despised, crushed and cut off from the living, the LORD speaks of him; Rashi, on 52:13 and 53:3, reads the servant as Jacob, all Israel spoken of as one man, whose righteous will prosper at the end of days.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Prophets, on Isaiah 52:13 and 53:3, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 56 to 60
days.key: Peace, peace, to him that is far off and to him that is near, Saith the LORD that createth the fruit of the lips; And I will heal him.
days.s: Having struck the covetous and seen his ways, the LORD promises comfort; Radak, on 57:19, hears peace in every mouth after the war of Gog and Magog, with war named no more, and the far and near as those far from Jerusalem and near it.
days.src: Radak, Commentary on Isaiah, on Isaiah 57:19, Hebrew (Radak on Nach), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Isaiah 61 to 65
days.key: In all their affliction He was afflicted, and the angel of His presence saved them; in His love and in His pity He redeemed them; And He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
days.s: Recounting the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel, the prophet recalls His care for them; Rashi, on 63:9, reading the written ‘not’, takes it as His not afflicting them as their deeds deserved, since Michael, prince of the Presence, always saved them, and Ibn Ezra, on 63:9, as His being distressed, as it were, and so hastening to save.
days.src: Rashi and Ibn Ezra, Commentaries on Isaiah, on Isaiah 63:9, Hebrew in Sefaria’s export 3f10136 (2026): Rashi, On Your Way; Ibn Ezra, Friedlander (1877)

days.label: Isaiah 66 to Jeremiah 2
days.key: Go, and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying: Thus saith the LORD: I remember for thee the affection of thy youth, the love of thine espousals; how thou wentest after Me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
days.s: After his call and two visions, Jeremiah is sent to speak to Jerusalem; Rashi, on Jeremiah 2:2, reads it as God longing to have mercy were they to return, remembering how they followed Moses and Aaron into the desert without provisions, trusting Him.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 2:2, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 3 to 5
days.key: For thus saith the LORD to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up for you a fallow ground, And sow not among thorns.
days.s: After the plea to Israel to return, the LORD turns to Judah and Jerusalem in a farmer’s image; Rashi, on 4:3, reads it as learning from farmers who plough in summer to kill the roots, and mending deeds before evil comes, lest prayer be rejected.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 4:3, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 6 to 8
days.key: Thus saith the LORD: Stand ye in the ways and see, And ask for the old paths, Where is the good way, and walk therein, And ye shall find rest for your souls.
days.s: Between the false cry of peace and the watchmen’s horn, the LORD bids the people seek the right road; Radak, on 6:16, reads it as two ways to know the good road, weighing it by reason and asking about past generations, by tradition.
days.src: Radak, commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 6:16, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “Radak on Nach”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 9 to 11
days.key: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth, and knoweth Me, That I am the LORD who exercise mercy, justice, and righteousness, in the earth; for in these things I delight, Saith the LORD.
days.s: Forbidding the wise, the mighty and the rich to boast, the LORD names the one ground for glory; Radak, on 9:23, reads understanding Him as grasping He is one and made all, and knowing Him as walking in His ways of mercy, justice and righteousness.
days.src: Radak, commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 9:23, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “Radak on Nach”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 12 to 14
days.key: Right wouldest Thou be, O LORD, were I to contend with Thee, yet will I reason with Thee: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? Wherefore are all they secure that deal very treacherously?
days.s: Opening a chapter in which even his own kin betray him, the prophet puts a question to the LORD; Rashi, on 12:1, reads him as knowing God will be right, yet arguing so that God will make His way known to him.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 12:1, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 15 to 17
days.key: Thus saith the LORD: Cursed is the man that trusteth in man, And maketh flesh his arm, And whose heart departeth from the LORD.
days.s: Setting a desert shrub against a watered tree, the chapter pronounces a curse; Radak, on 17:5, reads the curse as resting on the heart that turns away, for relying on a man is no evil if one holds he helps only by God’s aid.
days.src: Radak, commentary on Jeremiah, on Jeremiah 17:5, Hebrew (Sefaria’s “Radak on Nach”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 18 to 21
days.key: And if I say: ‘I will not make mention of Him, Nor speak any more in His name’, Then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire Shut up in my bones, And I weary myself to hold it in, But cannot.
days.s: After his night in Pashhur’s stocks, Jeremiah complains that the LORD’s word has made him a laughing-stock; Rashi, on 20:9, reads the fire as the prophecy itself, which compels him against his will to keep going on God’s mission.
days.src: Rashi, commentary on Jeremiah 20:9, Hebrew (On Your Way) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Jeremiah 22 to 23
days.key: He judged the cause of the poor and needy; Then it was well. Is not this to know Me? saith the LORD.
days.s: Rebuking a king who builds by unpaid labour, the prophet holds up his father, who did justice; Metzudat David, on 22:16, takes such judging as knowing God because by it he cleaves to God’s own deeds, pitying the poor as God does.
days.src: Metzudat David, commentary on Jeremiah 22:16, Hebrew (On Your Way) in Sefaria’s export, commit 3f10136 (2026)
